labels.notes: Unmarked, status partial. The Lean object is the printed relation: Causal.galileoLt U p q := p ∈ U ∧ p.1 < q.1 ∧ q ∈ connectedComponentIn U p (Causal/Galileo.lean:69) is ETT.tex:273-274 word for word. The le half adds p ∈ U, which the refutation does not use. galileo n = galileoOn (Fin n → ℝ) on ℝ × ℝⁿ. I checked the refutation by hand as well as through the kernel. U is the complement of the closed cup. p = (1/2, g 0) is joined to q = (2, g 0) in U by four segments ((s, g0) for s ∈ [-1, 1/2]; (-1, g s); (s, g 2); (2, g s)), none of which meets the cup. Over the cover {t > 1/4, t < 1/2}, a step in T₂ cannot start at t ≥ 1/2. A step in T₁ stays in the component of U ∩ T₁ through a, and U ∩ T₁ ⊆ P₁ ⊔ P₂, so that component lies in P₁ = {|f| < 1, t < 1}. So every chain from p stays in A = {|f| < 1, 1/2 ≤ t < 1}, while q.1 = 2. The paper's generation (lem:union_causalite, ETT.tex:367: links I⁺ in U ∩ U_i) matches Precausality.generated / AbsolutelyMinimalOn. galileo_not_minimal (n ≥ 1), galileo_not_hereditary, galileoOn_not_minimal (needs continuous f, g with f ∘ g = id), galileoOn_real_not_minimal and galileo_zero_hereditary / galileoOn_point_hereditary ([Subsingleton X]; instantiated at Fin 0 → ℝ, which is a singleton, so not vacuous) all state what the rows claim. The 'generated relation' reading is only raised (questions[0], 'Reading taken: none'). Under DEC-167 (every ETT causality is absolutely minimal) the finding holds in either form of OQ-95, since the form on M already fails. Citation: item 4 is ETT.tex:273-274 (275 is item 5's \item).

labels.label: cexemple:point_transparent
labels.notes: Unmarked, status partial. transparentLine (Causal/TransparentLine.lean:101) is the paper's relation. transparentLine_absolutelyMinimal (:276) gives the form on M, and transparentLine_not_hereditary := transparentLine_not_absolutelyMinimalOn (h realMinusZero), with realMinusZero = ℝ ∖ {0} (:284). The finding about 'This is a topological spacetime' is conditioned on the hereditary form ('Under the hereditary form …'), so OQ-95 is not decided. The sentence is at ETT.tex:478, not 477 (see findings). Among the concrete objects the transparent line is indeed the only one separating the two forms. The general claim is overstated (see findings).

build.details: Each of the seven files was compiled from lean-causal/ with `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true scaffold/CausalScaffold/GluingModels/<F>.lean`: rc 0 and no output for all seven. As a sanity check, a /tmp file holding a sorry fails with rc 1 under the same flag. The oleans of the seven modules and of CausalScaffold.GerochCauchy were present and newer than their sources. No lake build was run. `grep -c sorry` gives 0 in every file. Axioms were checked with a /tmp probe (outside the repository, deleted afterwards). It ran #print-axioms-style collectAxioms on all 250 declarations named in REPORT.json (inventory, labels, extra_decls, and the library lemmas cited in the notes): 249 give [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and 1 gives [propext, Quot.sound]. A sweep of all 128 constants under Causal.GluingModels (including auxiliary match_/eq_ constants) found SORRY 0 and NONSTD 0. That covers ModelScaffold's chronoMinkowski_hereditary and chronoMinkowski_minimal: they do not rest on GerochCauchy's tagged sorry (GerochCauchy.lean:788, theo:geroch). The only name the probe reported MISSING was one I had guessed myself (Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn.eq_of_discrete); the real name is Causal.AbsolutelyMinimalOn.eq_of_discrete.

findings.what: The sentence 'This is a topological spacetime' is at ETT.tex:478, not 477 (line 477 is blank). Galileo's item 4 is ETT.tex:273-274; line 275 is the \item of Minkowski space.

Two claims hold for the concrete objects only: 'the ONLY one on which the two forms of the gluing field differ' and 'Every other object that glues on M glues hereditarily'. The conditional constructions pass the separation on from their input. I proved in a /tmp probe (standard axioms) that withoutChronology transparentLine is AbsolutelyMinimal and not AbsolutelyMinimalOn realMinusZero, so it separates the two forms. The same holds for Gluing.causality, whose on-M lemma needs only the on-M form of its pieces. And chartedCausality D M is proved on M from hA alone, while its hereditary form also needs hGD (∀ e ∈ G, ChartIso D D e). The design step reads this note for OQ-95.
findings.fix: Say 'the only concrete object'. Add that for withoutChronology C, reflChrono C, Gluing.causality and chartedCausality the two forms follow the input (e.g. withoutChronology transparentLine separates them), and that chartedCausality's hereditary proof needs hGD.

findings.what: The hereditary column reads 'refuted' with no condition. The refutation holds only under the conditions the on-M column carries: T1, and x ≠ y with ¬ C.le ⊤ x y. When C already relates every pair on M, topEnlarge C has the same relations as C and may glue.
findings.fix: Write the hereditary status as 'refuted (T1, C.le ⊤ not total)', as in on_M.
